text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Liberals balk at PC rule changes: Opposition MPPs walk out, saying moves would limit debate, media coverage.
- CRTC adopts TV-show codes: Icons will warn parents of programs containing violence, sex or nudity.
- CBC-TV to update newscast at 11 p.m.
- Pol Pot's rebels say he's surrendered: Khmer Rouge leader in hands of ex-comrades, radio says.
- Jericho tale comes a-tumbling down: Archeological dig rebuts biblical story.
- Fingerprints leaving fingerprints of their own: Scientists say they can recover DNA from a year-old smudge and identify the person who left it.
- PanCanadian wins CS: White knight's C$465-million offer for heavy oil producer accepted, topping Gulf Canada's hostile bid.
- Manufacturing 'good news' boosts economy in April: Factory shipments, wholesale trade help erase March decline.
- New Kmart boss wants more sizzle for same old shelves: To focus on retailer's identity crisis.
- Pencer steals show at Cott meeting: Returns from brain surgery and leads a singalong.
- Fund manager sounds death knell for Hollinger's Southam offer.
- PanCanadian tops Gulf: Hostile bid by Gulf Canada gets steamrollered by PanCanadian's friendly offer of C$521 million for heavy oil producer CS Resources.
